title: Counterfactual Learning on Heterogeneous Graphs with Greedy Perturbation

problem.claim: Graph neural network predictions in high-stakes applications need interpretation, including for heterogeneous graphs.

gap.claim: Existing graph explanation methods do not ensure counterfactual validity and do not extend effectively to heterogeneous graphs.

contributions.claim: CF-HGExplainer is a counterfactual learning method for heterogeneous graphs.
The method uses semantic-aware attentive pooling and a heterogeneous decision-boundaries extraction module to identify common logic for similar graphs from classifier graph embeddings.
The method greedily perturbs nodes and edges using node-feature distributions and edge plausibility to train a neural network for heterogeneous edge-weight learning.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly present CF-HGExplainer as a novel counterfactual learning method for heterogeneous graphs.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments on two public academic datasets reportedly demonstrate the effectiveness of CF-HGExplainer against state-of-the-art methods for graph classification and graph interpretation.

narrative_sequence.summary: Interpretability is needed for graph neural networks used in high-stakes applications.
Existing explanation methods mainly generate important-edge subgraphs but have counterfactual-validity and heterogeneous-graph limitations.
The paper introduces CF-HGExplainer with semantic-aware pooling, decision-boundary extraction, and greedy node-edge perturbation for heterogeneous edge-weight learning.
The authors report extensive comparisons on two public academic datasets for graph classification and interpretation.

source_observation.claim: Existing explanations may identify important subgraphs without establishing that removing them changes the prediction.

interpretation.claim: Explanation quality should include a counterfactual validity check rather than importance alone.

application.claim: For graph explanations, test whether proposed structural changes produce the intended prediction change.

exception.claim: The abstract does not specify when counterfactual validity is unnecessary or how it is measured.

source_observation.claim: Heterogeneous graphs make interpretation difficult because of their complex information.

interpretation.claim: Interpretation methods may need semantic-aware mechanisms that account for heterogeneous graph structure and information.

application.claim: Use type- or semantic-aware representations when designing explanations for heterogeneous graph models.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether the approach generalizes beyond the reported heterogeneous graph classification and interpretation settings.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the two datasets, baselines, metrics, or quantitative results.
The abstract does not detail the model architecture, training procedure, or perturbation algorithm.
The abstract does not report limitations, computational costs, or failure cases.
